title: Search the product catalogue
summary: Search products by name or SKU, case-insensitive and partial, paginated with a total. A customer looking for the 50% Cotton Tee has to get the 50% Cotton Tee.

checkpoints.title: It matches part of a name, whatever the case
checkpoints.hint: ILIKE with the term wrapped in % on both sides. An absent or blank term is not a filter that matches everything, it is no filter at all.

checkpoints.title: A code that is nowhere in the name still finds the product
checkpoints.hint: or() over the two columns. Keep it one condition on one query: a product matching on both name and SKU is still one row.

checkpoints.title: A percent sign is a percent sign
checkpoints.hint: Parameterising the query stops SQL injection but does nothing about LIKE syntax: the value is still read as a pattern. Escape %, _ and the backslash itself before wrapping the term.

checkpoints.title: The pages line up with the total
checkpoints.hint: Total counts matches, so the count query needs the same filter as the page. Twelve products share a name, so ordering by name alone lets rows move between pages: order by something unique as well.

checkpoints.title: The rules hold on catalogues nobody wrote
checkpoints.hint: These catalogues stop the two searchable columns agreeing with each other: the awkward characters are in the SKU, SKUs carry mixed case with the searchable part in the middle rather than at the front, and a term can find one product by its name and a different one by its SKU. Read the first line of the report, because it names the rule that broke. If the rule is about the total, check that the count query filters on the same thing the page query does. If it is about a product on no page at all, check that one condition searches both columns rather than two queries being paged separately and merged.
